attendees.name_as_heard: Tanya Doll (also heard as Tanya Willard Doll)

budget_items.topic: Review of wage and salary schedules
budget_items.what_was_said: The bylaw requires the committee to review wage and salary schedules of all positions at a set interval and recommend action to the select board; members said comparable-town wage data has historically been hard to get accurately.

budget_items.topic: New hire starting pay / step approval
budget_items.what_was_said: New employees are to be hired at the minimum of the job's pay range unless the town manager, after consulting the chair, authorizes a higher step; the committee must formally vote to approve any new-hire pay above a stated step.

figures_as_heard: up to five days of vacation leave
budget_items.what_was_said: The plan lets the town manager offer recruitment incentives such as deposited vacation time or a sign-on bonus when hard-to-fill critical positions can't attract qualified applicants; the committee was unsure whether the town manager needs select board sign-off to use this.

Department heads must include a pay-adjustment section in their annual budget request, and any planned increase within the salary plan needs personnel committee approval before it goes into the budget; a member questioned whether step increases are actually automatic rather than discretionary.
Non-exempt employees get overtime at a stated multiplier of their regular rate for hours worked beyond a 40-hour week, counting paid leave time toward the 40 hours.

budget_items.topic: Compensatory time in lieu of overtime
budget_items.what_was_said: Employees may take compensatory time at the overtime rate instead of cash, but it must be used within a stated number of days.

Full-time employees accrue sick leave monthly up to a stated annual amount, cumulative up to a stated maximum, and it can be donated through a sick leave bank whose current status the committee was unsure of.

Employees who retire in good standing and were hired before a stated cutoff date get a percentage of accumulated unused sick leave paid out, rising with years of service; a member noted this only applies to employees hired before a certain date and few may still qualify.

budget_items.topic: Parental leave use of sick leave
budget_items.what_was_said: New parents may draw on a prorated cap of sick leave hours for parental leave.
Employees receive an annual longevity bonus as a percentage of salary starting after a stated years-of-service threshold, increasing at further milestones, paid each year on the anniversary date.

budget_items.topic: Pay upon transfer to a lower-graded job
budget_items.what_was_said: The committee discussed that an employee transferred to a lower-paying job could actually lose pay under the plan's placement formula, and planned to raise questions about it with counsel.

decisions.decision: Invite town counsel Attorney Terry and the HR director to the committee's next meeting (the 20th) to review bylaw language and roles.
Chair will ask the town's IT/facilities contact (Mason) about a portable meeting device (the 'owl') so meetings could move to other rooms.
Chair will compile a written list of the committee's questions for Attorney Terry and HR, to be sent ahead of the next meeting.
Committee will request copies of the recently finalized union contracts once available.
Committee will ask HR/town manager about the current status of the sick leave bank.
Committee will meet on the first and third Monday of each month going forward, and the chair will look into using the senior center or library as a more accessible meeting space.
Members will send any questions for Attorney Terry and HR to the chair by Monday the 13th so they can be answered in advance.

minutes.summary: This was the first meeting of Lunenburg's Personnel Committee since it was reactivated after being inactive since 2024; the three appointed members elected officers and then read through the town's salary administration plan bylaw section by section, flagging language they want clarified by town counsel and the HR director. No formal policy changes were voted; the committee set a recurring meeting schedule and agreed to bring a list of questions to its next meeting on the 20th.

what_happened.line: The reactivated Personnel Committee elected a chair, vice chair, and clerk by unanimous votes.
Members read through the town's salary administration bylaw section by section, taking no votes on policy changes.
The committee will invite town counsel and the HR director to its July 20 meeting to clarify bylaw language.
The committee flagged a bylaw provision that could reduce pay for an employee transferred to a lower-graded job.
The committee set a standing schedule of meetings on the first and third Monday of each month.

why_it_matters: Any pay adjustment within the salary plan needs this committee's approval before it enters a department's budget request, so its reviews reach the wage lines eventually voted at town meeting.
The bylaw under review sets new-hire starting pay, overtime and compensatory time, sick leave accrual and its payout at retirement, and longevity pay for every town employee.
The committee could not say what shape the sick leave bank currently takes and plans to ask the town manager for its status.
